## Why
A new name leaves a trail, in this order:

1. A lab or a well-followed account says it on X; a model enters Hugging Face's trending list.
2. On

e GitHub repo takes off on its own.
3. Directories and competitors add pages for it; someone registe

rs a domain for it and the site starts to rank.
4. Your own site gets its first search impressions f

or it.
5. Google Trends shows the curve, days or weeks later.
Keyword tools read step 5. This radar reads steps 1 to 4 every day and uses step 5 only to check its
ord tools read step 5. This radar reads steps 1 to 4 every day and uses step 5 only to check itself.

days later. People were searching "niko strata" from 9/26, while no second repo carried the name and

keyword tool listed it. A single repo gaining 800 stars a day is the whole signal, and it is public.

### When a source is missing or down
The table is still written, but it gets thinner, and it says which part is missing:
| What happens | What the table loses | The line it prints |
[该节后续省略]
### ⑥ Revenue: what people already pay for
A product that makes money proves the demand behind it. With `TRUSTMRR_API_KEY` set (from TrustMRR's
developer dashboard), the radar reads once a week (`revenue.weekday`, Monday by default) the 30 fas
test-growing products with at least `min_revenue_usd` ($500) in the last 30 days and the 30 newest l
istings, and keeps what it saw. The newest listings mostly earn next to nothing yet; they are read t
o record where they start, so a product at $0 last time that earns past the floor now is called out
first. Hidden listings ("Anonymous startup") are left out, and a company's legal name gives way to i
ts site's name ("Talent Tech Global Limited" is read as gptproto). Each product's own description go
es to the keyword table as evidence, so the table reads the job people pay for, not only the brand.
Growth above 1,000% reads "up from near $0": on the first run most of the fastest growers had starte
d from almost nothing.
TrustMRR's API terms forbid republishing its data and building public SEO pages from it. Use the lea
ds for your own research; do not publish the list.
### ⚡ What tutorial viewers ask for
For up to three leads a day marked ⚡ (a widely shared walkthrough of a manual workflow), the radar f
inds the top tutorial videos for the lead (GoAnyAPI), reads their comments (AIsa, $0.001 a page) and
has the model pull out what viewers ask for: the steps they find too hard, the "can this be done in
one click". That list is the one-click tool. It needs a GoAnyAPI key to find the videos.
